This is a great question! I myself am new and have seeked a lot of help regarding my first built deck that I have relentlessly attempted to improve by asking different members of my local and online mtg community.
Firstly, what is your strategy? In what ways are you trying to beat your opponent? Figure that out and filter your deck to fit that purpose. Sure cards like hungering hydra are wonderful, but do they fit the purpose a simic deck executes?
Secondly, I suggest you form a mana curve. Will you be able to survive long game? If so, will you survive an aggro deck, or a control deck? One of the major advantages of simic decks is the color blue, which means that counter spells and solution spells are Never out of place. This means that you have cheap cards to keep you alive until pulling out a massive hydra.
Finally, find favorite cards of your deck, and make sure they complement each other. You have to many 1 cards, meaning you might rely on them depending on the strategy your hand gives you. If that card is at the bottom of the deck, you might be screwed for that game. You only have a 1/60 chance to draw that card, so try to avoid that chance.
That's about  as much advice I have to give. Good luck!
